atoms.b: When speaking about climate, we mean the average conditions (such as temperature and rainfall) of a particular area over a ((++longer shorter)) period of time — usually about 30 years.
This is different to weather, which refers to the conditions of a particular area over a ((++shorter longer)) period of time.

atoms.text: Here in the UK, we have a temperate climate. This means that we have 4 distinct seasons and do not experience extreme temperature variations.
atoms.sound: Here in the UK, we have a temperate climate. This means that we have four-distinct seasons and do not experience extreme temperature variations.

atoms.text: In the summer, the temperature reaches up to 26 °C or higher and there is more sunshine.
Spring and autumn in the UK are generally cooler than summer. Average temperatures are usually between 8 °C and 17 °C. Flowers bloom in spring, and leaves fall from the trees in autumn.
Winter is the season with the coldest temperatures in the UK. While it is usually still quite mild, it can fall to 0 °C or lower, and there is sometimes snow.

atoms.b: The sea takes longer to heat up and cool down than land, so coastal regions have milder winters and cooler summers.
Depending on wind direction, a place can receive warmer or colder weather.
The higher a place is, the colder it is, because the air is thinner and holds less heat.
